title: OpenAI Astra 10-Problem Lean Release: Exponential Quantum Parallel Repetition, CVP Hardness & Connes Rigidity
aiSystem: Internal GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI) & Claude Fable 5 Reproductions
whyItMatters: For ~$2,000 in inference, OpenAI’s internal Astra delivered Lean-verified solutions to 10 decade-old problems—including Exponential Quantum Parallel Repetition, CVP lattice hardness, Connes rigidity, and Cohn–Elkies sphere packing.
summary: On August 1, 2026, OpenAI shocked the mathematics and theoretical computer science communities by releasing a 249-page manuscript and GitHub Lean 4 proof certificates generated by an internal version of GPT-6 Astra for ~$2,000 in total compute, resolving ten longstanding open problems (alongside Non-Sofic Groups). Standout results included an Exponential Quantum Parallel Repetition theorem for general two-player quantum games (solving Henry Yuen’s decade-old open problem via a novel resolvent purification and Uhlmann dilation), polynomial-factor hardness of approximation for the Closest Vector Problem (foundational to post-quantum lattice cryptography), a disproof of Connes’s rigidity conjecture in von Neumann algebras, 48-year-stuck high-dimensional sphere-packing bounds down to the Cohn–Elkies threshold, Ehrhart’s volume conjecture, n⁴/log n arithmetic-formula permanent lower bounds, and Erdős problems #146, #180, and #183. Within 24 hours, Levent Alpöge independently reproduced 5 of the 10 problems autonomously using Claude Fable 5.
technicalHighlights: Proved Exponential Quantum Parallel Repetition for general two-player quantum games—a decade-old flagship problem in quantum information theory.
Established polynomial-factor hardness of approximation for the Closest Vector Problem (CVP) without Unique Games, disproved Connes’s rigidity conjecture, and broke 48-year-old sphere-packing bounds.
Delivered all 10 solutions with Lean 4 certificates for ~$2,000 total inference cost; Claude Fable 5 independently reproduced 5 of the 10 within 24 hours.
caveats: While all ten shipped with Lean 4 certificates, specialist reviewers flagged missing prior-work attribution in a few manuscripts and noted that statement-fidelity and peer-review audits are still ongoing.

scoreRationale.foundational: Simultaneously broke through decade-old barriers in quantum complexity (QPR), lattice cryptography (CVP), operator algebras (Connes), and sphere packing.
scoreRationale.ripple: Widely recognized on LessWrong and across TCS/math as the inflection point proving frontier LLMs had crossed into superhuman multi-domain theorem proving.
scoreRationale.verification: All ten results shipped with Lean 4 certificates and 5 were independently reproduced within 24 hours by Claude Fable 5, though full human peer review continues.
scoreRationale.velocity: Resolved ten major multi-decade open problems for ~$2,000 in total compute.
